# Okra

<!-- BEGIN: hmi-opening -->
<div class="hmi-quick-read">
  <div class="hmi-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>
  <p>Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic and total mercury in okra are reported as monitoring results, studies, references by form and basis, limits, testing and controls.</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Metals of concern:</strong> the metals named by the studies cited on this page.</li>
    <li><strong>Main drivers:</strong> form, origin and preparation stay separate.</li>
    <li><strong>Practical framing:</strong> this page does not pool those studies into one typical value.</li>
  </ul>
</div>

This page draws on evidence from [[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|WHO]], together with 8 peer-reviewed studies. The complete citation list is at the bottom of the page.
<!-- END: hmi-opening -->

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-okra" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-okra-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of okra, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>32</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for okra, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for okra, as sold on this basis in the completed okra ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. In one study, chromium across 4 groups of okra ranged from 200 µg/kg (sampling phase 4, Kawran Bazar, Dhaka) to 1,100 µg/kg (sampling phase 2, Kawran Bazar, Dhaka); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/sultana2021-dhaka-kawran-bazar-fruit-vegetables-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sultana R, Chamon AS, Mondol MN, Tasnim I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sultana2021-dhaka-kawran-bazar-fruit-vegetables-metals">Metal concentration in commonly sold fruit vegetables in Dhaka city market and probable health risk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Dhaka University Journal of Biological Sciences 30(1):35-47</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sultana2021-dhaka-kawran-bazar-fruit-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in okra is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 5 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Laizu J · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation">Speciation of arsenic in vegetables and their correlation with inorganic phosphate level</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Pharmacology 2007;
